items.question: what does this mean?
items.script:
say This is a matrix equation: a 2 by 2 matrix times a vector equals a vector.
highlight 380 175 390 140 | matrix times vector equals vector
say Think of it like a recipe: the numbers on the left mix together to give the numbers on the right.
say The lecturer is solving for x and y, the two unknowns, by combining the equations.
title Matrix form of a linear system, Ax = b

items.question: explain this like a story
items.script:
clear
say Once upon a time, two friends had a puzzle: find two mystery numbers, x and y.
highlight 380 175 390 140 | the puzzle on the board
say The first clue was: two times x, minus y, gives zero.
say The second clue was: x plus two times y gives three.
say Together, the clues make a team, and the lecturer is combining them to crack the code.
title Solving a linear system like a story

items.question: show me step by step how to solve this
items.script:
clear
say Let's solve it step by step. The board gives two equations.
highlight 380 175 390 140 | the two equations
say Step 1: From the first equation, 2x minus y equals 0, so y equals 2x.
say Step 2: Put 2x in place of y in the second equation: x plus 2 times 2x equals 3, so 5x equals 3.
say Step 3: So x is 3/5, and y is 2 times 3/5, which is 6/5. Check: both equations work.
title Solving a 2 by 2 linear system by substitution

items.question: how would they test this, exam style?
items.script:
clear
say An exam might give you a similar 2 by 2 system and ask you to solve it.
highlight 380 175 390 140 | this kind of question
say Example: 3x plus y equals 7, and x minus y equals 1. Find x and y.
say Start by adding the two equations to remove y: 4x equals 8, so x is 2 and y is 1.
say Always check your answer by putting both numbers back into both equations.
title Exam-style practice: solving 2 by 2 systems

items.question: quiz me on this
items.script:
clear
say Quick quiz. Using the board's system, what is x?
highlight 380 175 390 140 | the system we solved
choices 3/5 | 1 | 0
say Pick one, and tell me why you chose it.

items.question: what is a matrix?
items.script:
clear
say A matrix is a neat box of numbers, arranged in rows and columns.
highlight 380 175 200 140 | the box of numbers
say Think of it like a seating chart: each number has its own row and column spot.
say On the board, the matrix has two rows and two columns, so it is called a 2 by 2 matrix.
title What is a matrix?

items.question: why do we write it as a matrix?
items.script:
clear
say Writing a matrix is a shortcut, like a tidy table instead of a long list.
highlight 330 170 450 160 | the whole system in one box
say Instead of writing two equations, we write one line: A times x equals b.
say This makes big systems, with many unknowns, much easier to work with.
say The same tools, like elimination, work on the matrix, so the math stays neat.
title Why write a linear system as a matrix

items.question: what does the x mean here?
items.script:
clear
say Here x is not one number. It is a list of the unknowns, x and y, stacked up.
highlight 370 200 50 60 | the vector x
say Think of it like a shopping list: x holds the two mystery amounts we want to find.
say When you multiply the matrix by x, you get the left side of both equations at once.
title What x means in Ax = b

items.question: what is a system of linear equations?
items.script:
<reasoning_effort>8</reasoning_effort>
clear
say A system of linear equations is a group of equations that share the same unknowns.
highlight 330 170 450 160 | the two equations together
say Think of two friends sharing one bill: both clues must be true at the same time.
say On the board, the two equations use the same x and y, so we solve them together.
title What is a system of linear equations?

items.question: can you visualize this?
items.script:
clear
say Yes. Each equation is a line on a graph, and the answer is where the two lines cross.
highlight 330 170 450 160 | two lines, one crossing point
say Line one is y equals 2x. Line two is x plus 2y equals 3.
say They cross at x equals 0.6 and y equals 1.2. That single point solves both equations.
say Think of two roads on a map: the meeting point is the one spot both roads share.
title Visualizing a linear system as crossing lines

items.question: explain this diagram
items.script:
clear
say This is a neural network reading a handwritten digit, here a 2.
highlight 330 90 50 470 | input: 784 pixel brightnesses
say The 784 numbers come from a 28 by 28 pixel image, one number per pixel.
highlight 470 120 130 420 | hidden layers pass signals along
arrow 370 300 -> 690 300 | information flows left to right
highlight 690 200 50 260 | output: one score per digit 0 to 9
say The network picks the output with the highest score, here the 2.
title How a neural network reads digits

items.question: what are these circles?
items.script:
clear
say These circles are neurons. Each one holds a single number, shown by how bright it is.
ring 470 190 22 | one neuron
say Think of a neuron like a dimmer switch: it gets numbers from the left and decides how bright to glow.
say Brighter circles mean a bigger number, so the network is more confident about that signal.
title What are neurons in a neural network?

items.question: what do the lines between them mean?
items.script:
clear
say The lines are connections, and each one has a weight: a number that sets how strong the signal is.
arrow 480 200 -> 580 240 | one connection with a weight
say Think of each line as a volume knob: turn it up and that signal gets louder.
say During training, the network adjusts all these weights until the right digit wins.
title What the connections (weights) mean

items.question: how does a neural network learn?
items.script:
clear
say The network learns by practice: it guesses, checks how wrong it was, and adjusts its weights.
highlight 690 200 50 260 | the guess gets compared to the right answer
say Think of learning darts: after each throw, you nudge your aim a little toward the bullseye.
say Gradient descent is the method that finds the direction to nudge every weight at once.
say Repeat this over thousands of handwritten digits, and the weights settle into good values.
title How a neural network learns: gradient descent

items.question: explain this like a story
items.script:
clear
say Once upon a time, a tiny robot named Digit wanted to learn to read handwriting.
highlight 45 88 145 146 | the handwritten 2 it sees
say Each time it looked at a picture, it made a guess, and the teacher said how far off it was.
say After every mistake, it turned its little knobs, the weights, a tiny bit toward the right answer.
say After thousands of pictures, Digit could spot a 2 in a blink, just like you do.
title How a neural network learns, as a story

items.question: quiz me on neural networks
items.script:
clear

highlight 690 200 50 260 | the output layer
choices a score for each digit 0 to 9 | one single pixel | the original image

items.question: what is the input layer?
items.script:
clear
say The input layer is where the picture goes in: one neuron for each of the 784 pixels.
highlight 330 90 50 470 | the input layer
say Think of it like a grid of tiny lights, where each light shows how bright one pixel is.
say The 784 comes from a 28 by 28 image, because 28 times 28 equals 784.
title The input layer of a neural network

items.question: what is gradient descent?
items.script:
clear
say Gradient descent is a way to find the lowest point of a mistake score, step by step.
highlight 15 608 495 26 | this video covers gradient descent
say Imagine walking down a hill in thick fog. You can't see the bottom, but you can feel which way is downhill.
say Each step, the network checks the slope of its error and moves its weights a little downhill.
say Keep taking small steps, and the error gets smaller, until the network is good at digits.
title Gradient descent: walking downhill to lower the error

items.question: what is the output here?
items.script:
clear
say The output is the 10 circles on the right, one for each digit from 0 to 9.
highlight 690 200 50 260 | the 10 output neurons
say The brightest output circle is the network's answer. Here, the picture is a 2, so the 2 should win.
say Think of a multiple choice test: each option gets a score, and the network picks the highest one.
title The output layer: picking the digit

items.question: show me visually how information flows
items.script:
clear
say Information flows left to right, one layer at a time.
arrow 365 300 -> 460 300 | pixels go in
say The first hidden layer mixes the pixels into simple shapes like edges.
arrow 480 300 -> 580 300 | shapes pass to the next layer
say The second hidden layer combines shapes into parts, like loops and lines.
arrow 600 300 -> 690 300 | scores reach the output
say The output layer gives a score for each digit, and the top score wins.
title How information flows through a neural network

items.question: explain how video streaming works
items.script:
clear
say Streaming means the video is sent in small pieces, not as one big file.
highlight 28 530 910 10 | the bar shows what is buffered
say Think of a conveyor belt: chunks arrive in order, and you watch them as they land.
say Your player downloads a little ahead, called buffering, so the video keeps playing smoothly.
title How video streaming works

items.question: what is a variable in python?
items.script:
clear
say A variable in Python is a labeled box that holds a value.
say Think of a sticky label on a jar: the label is the name, and the jar holds the value.
say For example, writing age = 15 stores the number 15 under the name age.
title Variables in Python

items.question: explain recursion
items.script:
clear
say Recursion means a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem.
say Think of Russian nesting dolls: open one, and inside is a smaller doll of the same kind.
say Every recursive function needs a base case, a simple answer that stops the calling.
say For example, factorial of 3 is 3 times factorial of 2, until it reaches factorial of 1, which is 1.
title Recursion: a function that calls itself

items.question: what is an API?
items.script:
clear
say An API is a set of rules that lets one program ask another program for something.
say Think of a restaurant menu: you pick a dish, the kitchen makes it, and you never enter the kitchen yourself.
say The menu is the API, the waiter carries your order, and the kitchen does the work behind the scenes.
say For example, a weather app calls a weather service's API to get today's temperature.
title What is an API?

items.question: what is compound interest?
items.script:
clear
say Compound interest is interest earned on your money plus the interest you already earned.
say Think of a snowball rolling downhill: it picks up more snow, so it grows faster each time.
say For example, 100 taka at 10 percent becomes 110, then the next year 10 percent of 110 is added.
title Compound interest: interest on interest

items.question: how do I solve 2x + 3 = 11?
items.script:
clear
say Step 1: Subtract 3 from both sides, so 2x equals 8.
say Step 2: Divide both sides by 2, so x equals 4.
say Check: 2 times 4 is 8, plus 3 is 11. It works.
title Solving a one-step-then-two-step equation

items.question: what is the derivative of x squared?
items.script:
clear
say The derivative of x squared is 2x.
say Think of it as the slope of the curve: how steep the x squared graph is at each point.
say The rule is simple: bring the power down in front, then lower the power by one.
title The derivative of x squared
